desk_read: Yesterday's session showed a clear divergence between energy markets and equities or metals. WTI Crude Oil saw prices gain +1.99% alongside a total open interest increase of +9.7k contracts (+0.8%), driven by new longs while maintaining backwardation. Meanwhile, Brent NYMEX rose +2.10% with total open interest dropping -1.4k contracts (-1.1%) as an expiry roll took place. In contrast, Nasdaq 100 drifted lower by -0.67% while total open interest expanded by +5.8k contracts (+1.8%), pointing to new shorts. Natural Gas experienced long liquidation alongside a price decline of -0.14% and a total open interest reduction of -11.0k contracts (-0.8%).
oil_read: XenosFinance Oil Desk Note: WTI CLF27 rose +1.99% with total open interest up +9.7k contracts (+0.8%), volume at 0.9x its 20-day average, and a flow read of new longs in backwardation with the CLF27-CLM27 spread at +6.33 $/bbl. Brent BZG27 gained +2.10% while total open interest fell -1.4k contracts (-1.1%) and volume printed 0.5x its 20-day average, showing an expiry roll flow read in backwardation with the BZG27-BZM27 spread at +7.32 $/bbl.
bias_read: WTI Crude Oil is bullish with new longs and a steepening backwardation, while Brent is mildly bullish on light volume 0.5x the 20-day average, meaning Brent lacks the conviction to confirm WTI's strength. Nasdaq 100 shows a mildly bearish bias from new shorts, supporting downside pressure. Meanwhile, Silver and Copper sit at mildly bearish with long liquidation on volume 1.4x the 20-day average and 1.5x the 20-day average respectively, warning of trend exhaustion rather than durable selling. Across markets, positioning is mixed and largely unsupportive of aggressive directional extensions.
